description: Princess Kay and her court each have their likenesses carved into a 90-pound block of butter by sculptor Gerry Kulzer. This tradition, dating back to 1965, honors contestants in the Midwest Dairy Princess Kay of the Milky Way competition. These young women serve as the goodwill ambassadors for Minnesota’s dairy farmers. Princess Kay’s likeness is carved over the first two days of the fair, followed by one of the finalists’ likenesses carved each day of the fair through Labor Day. The princess being sculpted and the sculptor rotate in a 40° display cooler and periodically answer questions from the audience. After the fair, each contestant takes home their sculpture to enjoy for years to come. Stop by the southeast corner of the Dairy Building to experience this udder-ly unique form of art!
name: Butter Sculptures

description: Unique to the Minnesota State Fair, crop art originated in 1965 and has been a cherished tradition since. Each art piece is made from Minnesota-grown seeds, stems and other plant parts on supporting backgrounds with or without the use of paints and dyes. Works of art entered in this year’s competition, as well as pieces by renowned crop artists, are on display all 12 days of the fair. Each year the crop art competition garners nearly 700 entries and continues to “grow.” Stop by the Agriculture Horticulture Building to marvel at these crop-tastic creations!
name: Crop Art Exhibit

description: Take a stroll through the butterfly house and get up close with these winged wonders. Watch them zip around, land on flowers, and maybe even on you! It's a peaceful escape and a perfect chance to learn about their life cycle and the environment they thrive in.
